summary: A cab-topped lookout on private land in Greene County, Indiana, standing in poor repair, with its cab roof and floor gone, and not open to visitors.

facts.design: Tower with a cab on top; wooden stairs and landings (register)
facts.status_note: Standing, but in poor repair: the cab has lost its roof and floor, and the register says climbing is unsafe.

access.note: On private property, not public land. The register says visiting without landowner permission is illegal.

visit.trail_note: No public access. The Indiana Fire Towers author visited in June 2024, could not get right up to the tower because it is not on public property, and could see it from a few directions.

events.note: A September 1939 magazine article is read by Indiana Fire Towers as implying the tower already stood then. The register dates the build to before 1940.
Visit in June 2024 (Indiana Fire Towers): cab in horrible condition; not climbable; not on public land.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on August 2, 2026.

evidence.quote: Private property; southwest of Bloomington Indiana.

the wood planks on the tower's various landings are rotten as well.

notes_for_editor: The build year and builder are unknown. The register says before 1940, and the 1939 magazine point is an inference from the Indiana Fire Towers site, so the story says 'implying'. Ownership is disputed: the register says state-leased land, while Indiana Fire Towers is unsure it was ever state property; the story shows both. The June 2024 visit sentence now carries footnote 2, and the 'outside the property' wording was replaced with what the author actually wrote (not on public property, could not get right up to it). Unread lead: a 2022 FFLA Indiana chapter report by Teena Ligman, linked from the Indiana Fire Towers page, which the site says has a story and pictures of this tower. The access line is private: the register says visiting without permission is illegal, so do not invite visits. No photos added; the NHLR photos stay in the record.
